written.headline: Trump administration weighs forcing US firms to disclose Chinese AI use
written.summary: The Trump administration is considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models on their websites. The plan, discussed by the Treasury Department and the White House, aims to discourage reliance on Chinese AI without imposing outright restrictions.

written.headline: Google selects Blue Origin to launch Project Suncatcher AI satellites in 2029
written.summary: Google selected Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket to launch satellites for Project Suncatcher, an experiment testing AI computing in space. The mission is targeted for the first quarter of 2029.

written.headline: Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq at $1.5 trillion valuation after $81.34 billion IPO
written.summary: Anthropic went public on Nasdaq after raising USD 81.34 billion in an initial public offering that valued the company at approximately USD 1.5 trillion. CEO Dario Amodei stated that the company will prioritize safety and human control over business or political pressures.

written.headline: Signal restricts screenshots to block AI agents from reading messages
written.summary: Encrypted messaging service Signal introduced default restrictions on screenshots to prevent device-level AI agents from reading private chats. The company warned that operating system integrations by tech giants pose an existential threat to its privacy guarantee.

written.headline: Analysis of 10M job ads in China shows double-digit decline for AI-exposed roles
written.summary: An analysis of 10 million job advertisements in China between 2021 and 2025 revealed a double-digit decline in listings for roles with high AI exposure compared to less-exposed positions. The study highlights a growing impact of artificial intelligence on hiring trends in the region.

written.headline: Travis Kalanick backs Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
written.summary: Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick stated he would support the return of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Kalanick remarked he would bring a wafer-encrusted megaphone to Nvidia's headquarters to back Huang's reinstatement.
